problem.statement: Distilling a change into an Intent Document took minutes of wall clock and repeated full-document resubmits. Profiling three real runs found the cost was almost entirely mechanical: an interview filed under a key the submit never read, consent discovered after the document existed, and an author navigating a transcript blind.
user_asks: In the review assist, the time it takes to build that intent document is high and labourious. How can we reduce the time.
We need to make this part deterministic to avoid bad rounds and reduce the overall back and forth
my problem was with the overall data in the final intent document having too much jargon and not being easy to skim through
Generate separate parsers for codex and claude.. make sure we create necessary interfaces and used solid principles
out_of_scope: A scan layer in the renderer

assumptions.assumption: A session's conversation fits one read.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The author is back to retrieving, and search is gone.

assumptions.assumption: Requiring run_id makes the lost-interview bug unreachable.
assumptions.how_to_verify: End-to-end: an omitted run_id is refused with MCP error -32602.

assumptions.assumption: A subagent transcript holds no developer intent.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Reasoning in delegated work is dropped from every document.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Check whether any trial in a real document traces only to a subagent.

assumptions.assumption: The rewritten prompts produce better documents.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The mechanical costs are gone and the output reads the same.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Run a two-role distillation and read what comes out.

open_questions.question: Does generation actually take less time?
open_questions.context: Unmeasured. The 8.5 minutes profiled was model latency across two role subagents; everything verified here is server-side I/O.

open_questions.question: Can a cloud Cowork session ever be distilled?
open_questions.context: Its transcript never reaches the developer's machine, so the author has nothing to hydrate from - including for this very document.

requirements.text: Make round recording deterministic rather than advisory
Separate parsers per agent, behind interfaces, SOLID
Fix jargon and skimmability, not length

trials.what: Character budgets on assumptions and tour fields, enforced by the validator
trials.why_abandoned: 125 of 190 fields in real documents violated them, and the longest field was the most valuable content in its document. A rule two-thirds of real output breaks is miscalibrated.

trials.what: A git-derived context hint on every hunk
trials.why_abandoned: Present on 80% of hunks but uninformative exactly where the preview was, and it needed a caveat everywhere it was mentioned.

trials.what: Detecting dispatcher sessions by subagent-to-parent prose ratio
trials.why_abandoned: Built from a single outlier. A subagent has no human in the loop, so it can hold no ask, plan or decision regardless of size.

trials.what: Chunking the conversation and searching annotations
trials.why_abandoned: 40 of 41 sessions fit whole in one read, so the retrieval problem the design solved does not exist at this scale.

trials.what: A literal-string find tool to replace ranked search
trials.why_abandoned: The spine's indices already reach the evidence, and no measured case needed more.

adopted.summary: Identify a distillation by a content-addressed run, key interview rounds by question, hand the author the whole conversation in one call, and number the hunks so a tour stop can name them.
adopted.rationale: Every failure in the traces was mechanical, so the fixes are mechanical: required arguments instead of defaulted ones, idempotent recording instead of append, and one complete read instead of retrieval. Search was deleted rather than improved because a map removes the need to hunt.

tour.title: Interview answers were filed where nothing would look for them
tour.what: Identifies a distillation by a hash of the change and stores its rounds on disk, keyed by question.
tour.why: Rounds were filed under the working directory while the submit looked under the repository, so a reviewer asked the same questions three times and re-sent the same document four times.
tour.attention: that a retried question replaces rather than appends.

tour.title: The tools now demand the run rather than guessing at it
tour.what: Threads the run handle through diff, interview and submit, and reports consent when the run opens.
tour.why: An argument with a plausible default was omitted and the loss surfaced minutes later; required, the same mistake is refused immediately.
tour.attention: whether every path that writes still resolves its repo from the run.

tour.title: The whole conversation, in one read
tour.what: Reduces a session to what was said, with commands and edits as one-liners and everything else marked by index.
tour.why: A session is a median 4.8% conversation; the author was pulling more than that in scattered pieces and still missing things.
tour.attention: that a gap marker never hides a failure.

tour.title: Claude Code and Codex read by their own parsers
tour.what: One interface, one implementation per agent, routed by entry shape.
tour.why: Shared guessing half-worked in silence: 831 Codex entries collapsed to a single item and every Codex preview came back blank.
tour.attention: that neither parser claims the other's entries.

tour.title: Hunks get short names so a stop can point at them
tour.what: Numbers every hunk and lets an anchor be a name instead of four line numbers.
tour.why: Anchors were the one part of authoring that rewarded transcription over judgement, and a wrong number cost a full re-emission.
tour.attention: that ids never reach the stored document.

tour.title: Installing role definitions now removes the ones it replaces
tour.what: Sweeps definitions this server wrote, trims the reviewer's tools, and generates each prompt's access list.
tour.why: A project-scoped copy shadows the user-scoped one, so sessions ran month-old prompts while the server reported installing current ones.
tour.attention: that a hand-written file is never deleted.

tour.title: Only sessions a human was present for
tour.what: Returns parent sessions, counts the turns a human typed, and takes previews from the parsers.
tour.why: Subagent transcripts were offered as sessions in their own right, and Codex sub-agent runs look like ordinary sessions on disk.
tour.attention: whether user_turns can read zero for a real session.

tour.title: Prompts rewritten around reading, converging and provenance
tour.what: Rewrites both role prompts and the guide: read the conversation once, close every round, say where each field came from, write the tour for someone deciding where to look.
tour.why: The author was told to page a transcript that no longer needs paging, and the field that tells a reviewer what to check was filled on 8 of 40 stops because nothing asked for it.
tour.attention: that no prompt names a tool that no longer exists.

tour.title: Packaging and test config
tour.what: Manifest tool list, a test script, and a vitest text loader.
tour.why: The loader is not housekeeping: role prose lives in files esbuild inlines, so the prompts could not be imported under test at all.

performed.description: 85 unit tests across runs, spine, parsers, roles, selection, hunks and the validator
stdio end-to-end against the built server: run handle, idempotent rounds, hunk-id anchors, consent gate
buildSpine over 40 real sessions in one workspace

not_verified: That generation is faster. No two-role distillation has been run; the 8.5 minutes profiled was model latency.
That the rewritten prompts produce better documents. This one was written in a single pass with no author/reviewer split.
That a cloud Cowork session can be distilled at all - its transcript is not on the developer's machine, including for this change.
